thread:
kevin: Heads up — noticed Console dashboards are much slower after yesterday's frontend deploy. Landing page TTI jumped for a bunch of customers :eyes:

sara: saw it too, internal page load alerts spiked around 09:12 UTC. Users reporting charts take ages to show up.

josh: p95 TTI from our synthetic monitors: 2.2s -> 9.1s after the release. CPU on client side pegged during hydration.

kevin: attaching the lighthouse snippet from a repro run:
```
First Contentful Paint: 2.1s
Largest Contentful Paint: 3.9s
Time to Interactive: 8.7s
Total JS transfer: 1.8 MB
Main thread blocking time: 360 ms
```

anita: summary from perf-bot trace: heavy JS parse/compile from bundle: charts + vega-like utils + new telemetry SDK import all in main chunk. trace: https://perf.example.com/trace/abc123

perf-bot: auto-detected large module: node_modules/complex-chart/ => 420KB parsed, no code-splitting.

zane: that charting lib was added to improve legend interactions. The package pulls in a ton of d3 submodules. We accidentally imported it in console/AppLayout so it loads before route split.

josh: repro steps I used:
1) clear cache
2) open /dashboards at cold start
3) open Chrome trace -> CPU main thread shows long parse/compile at t=0.

anita: quick fix options:
- revert the package bump (fast rollback)
- lazy-load chart component via dynamic import and show skeleton/placeholder first
- ship tiny custom render for initial list view and hydrate charts on idle

kevin: we should avoid rollback if we can patch with lazy-load today. Can we land a canary to 5%? @maria

maria: yes, we can cut a traffic % rollout in the console feature-flagging service. I can do 5% canary once a patch is ready.

zane: prototype patch: move import out of AppLayout -> dynamic import inside DashboardChart wrapper:
```js
// before
import ComplexChart from 'complex-chart';
// after
const ComplexChart = React.lazy(() => import('complex-chart'));
```
plus show lightweight svg placeholder until loaded.

anita: also recommend deferring telemetry SDK init on first paint. We added a new telemetry wrapper that waits for immediate metrics and it blocks some microtasks. Defer to requestIdleCallback for non-critical sends.

josh: curious if tree-shaking could help: looks like we import `complex-chart/legacy` somewhere in utils — might be bringing polyfills. Will audit imports.

perf-bot: note: shipping dynamic import will require updating our CSP and chunk host config. Create a quick change to webpack chunkPrefix and ensure SRI settings preserved.

kevin: good call. Anita, zane — can you collaborate on PR with lazy-load + telemetry defer? Josh to audit imports and try to shave 100-200KB. Maria to do 5% canary config after PR merged. I'll monitor metrics.

anita: will open PR today. plan:
- lazy-load heavy chart component + placeholder (anita)
- telemetry init defer + batch API (anita)
- import audit & prune unused d3 bits (josh)
- update build to keep vendor split consistent (zane)

kevin: what telemetry metric do we use to gate rollback? we need a quick alert rule.

maria: we have a custom metric: console.render.time_to_interactive. I can set a canary alert threshold: >6s for 5% will auto-suspend rollout.

zane: also adding memoization on series render and using requestIdleCallback to decode big CSV -> JSON in a web worker if possible. That's low-risk and buys time.

josh: re: web worker — there's shared state we need to serialize, but decoding can be fully off-main-thread. I'll prototype a small worker and measure.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-06-10T09:05:31Z succeeded for feature/frontend-charts-lazy (sha abcdef).

anita: PR 4382 opened: lazy-load complex-chart, defer telemetry init, placeholder skeleton. Size delta: main chunk -380KB, new chunk ~420KB. Still testing.

perf-bot: running synthetic against canary (5%)... first batch shows p75 TTI down to 4.2s on canary, p95 still 6.8s. baseline 9.1s.

kevin: nice. still want p95 < 6s. Next: josh to remove legacy imports, zane to add worker decode.

josh: removed legacy import in utils. main -120KB. Updated PR 4382 with commit.

zane: worker prototype added in a follow-up commit — decodes CSV off-main-thread and posts ready data. That shaved another ~400ms in local runs.

maria: canary metrics look stable for 10 minutes. I'll hold at 5% and increase to 25% if no regressions. Alert configured.

kevin: schedule: patch -> canary 5% now -> observe 30m -> 25% -> 100% if green. Owners: anita/zane/josh. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sara: documenting troubleshooting steps and perf dashboard query in #eng-platform/perf-runbook.

kevin: leaving this thread open but moving action items to the PR. If anything spikes, ping me and I'll rollback the feature-flag.

maria: note for postmortem: include why import landed in AppLayout and add a lint rule to prevent route-global imports of heavy chart libs.

kevin: agreed — adding lint rule ticket after rollout.

perf-bot: summary: main chunk reduced by ~500KB, TTI p95 improved from 9.1s -> 5.9s on canary.
